assumptions.summary: In every one of the n rounds of the run an acceptance value of the alphabet is recorded. The counts and the frequency vector then describe the whole run, normalised by its round count.
assumptions.title: An acceptance value recorded in every round
assumptions.user_statement: Every one of the n rounds of your run records an acceptance value from the declared acceptance alphabet: no round counted in n is missing from the record. If rounds go missing (for example through lost time tags), the counts are normalised against the wrong number of rounds and the acceptance test does not describe the run. A round missing from the record also puts security at stake: the acceptance test must be evaluated on the acceptance values of all n rounds ([[A-CONFORM]]), and a measured round the record drops is a sifting step the declaration does not describe ([[A-SPEC]]). Where the engine builds the acceptance set, it checks that the alphabet, its order and n are those of your protocol declaration; a set carried in the declaration is read in the declaration's order, so writing it in that order is yours to check.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Every classical message travels through an authentication scheme using at most k_auth bits of pre-shared key and realising the authenticated classical channel within ε_auth, a reused key's distance from an ideal one included. It is the premise by which authentication enters the key's security.
assumptions.title: Authentication of the classical channel by a keyed scheme
assumptions.user_statement: Every classical message of your protocol, per-round announcements included, is protected by one authentication scheme: the attacker may read, delay or block any message, but one she alters or injects, or delivers before it was sent, is rejected except within an error ε_auth. It uses at most k_auth bits of pre-shared secret key per run. That error is its composable error on two identical copies of a uniform, independent key plus the distance of the parties' actual copies from such a pair (zero for a fresh key; for a key from an earlier run, a distance you must bound, which that run's security parameter alone does not bound); declare that sum as ε_auth and the bits used as k_auth. No composable proof for this timing-aware channel is published yet; Wegman–Carter authentication with separate keys per direction approximates it. Both declared zero assert a keyless authenticated channel.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Every public choice is drawn with its declared bias; those of fixed bias are jointly independent of each other, the quantum systems and the adversary, and one weighted by a station's setting depends on the round through that setting only. It lets a weight inside the measurement describe the round.
assumptions.title: Public choices as private coins of declared bias
assumptions.user_statement: Every public choice of your protocol (for example an actively chosen basis, or whether a round is a test round; a basis set passively by a beam splitter is part of the measurement, not a choice), whichever party draws it and at whichever of its stations, comes from a local random number generator with exactly the declared probabilities, and each is announced or kept secret exactly as declared. The choices with fixed probabilities are independent of each other and, all together, of the quantum signals and of anything an attacker does. A choice whose probabilities depend on a station's private setting is drawn by a party whose recorded outcome includes that setting, and may depend on that setting only, never otherwise on Alice's letter, another choice or a detection result.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The implementation applies the acceptance test and the verification abort, sends no message beyond the model's, outputs the model's key or nothing, uses no key before the execution ends and aborts on an authentication failure. It ties the analysed protocol to the one that runs.
assumptions.title: The implementation runs the analysed post-processing
assumptions.user_statement: Your implementation runs exactly the analysed post-processing. It aborts unless the acceptance statistics lie in the declared acceptance set; after the rounds it sends no public message other than the error-correction transcript of at most λ_EC bits and its seed, the verification seed, hash and result, the privacy-amplification hash choice and the closing accept or abort decisions; it aborts when verification fails or a message fails authentication (an auth-abort); it outputs the analysed ℓ-bit key, or nothing. No part of the key is used before the execution has ended: the key holder, having sent its final decision, waits until the partner has received it or an auth-abort in its place, and the partner until one of these has arrived. Interactive error correction, a resent syndrome or early key use violate this. Tightening 2ε_auth to ε_auth under this timing is an open question.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The physical source draws each round's letter independently with the declared weights and emits the product of the declared states, no round depending on another. It ties a source specification declared as matrices to the device it describes.
assumptions.title: Emission of the specified ensemble
assumptions.user_statement: Your source prepares, in every round, one of the declared states with the declared probabilities. Each round's letter is drawn independently with weights p_x, and the states emitted over the n rounds form a product: no round's letter or state depends on another round, its detection results or its public messages. A source with memory or drift between rounds (for example pattern effects in a modulator) violates this. Where your source is a pair source inside your laboratory with one half measured there to herald or fix the letter, those local detectors belong to the declared ensemble: their efficiency mismatch must be carried by the declared weights and states, and their memory across rounds (for example afterpulsing or dead time) violates this like any other dependence between rounds.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The acceptance set, the round count, the key length, the transcript length, the error budgets, the authentication parameters and the Rényi order are fixed before the run and applied unchanged. The key length is that of a fixed-length protocol, not one chosen from the run's data.
assumptions.title: Protocol parameters fixed before the run
assumptions.user_statement: Every parameter the key length rests on is fixed before the run starts: the acceptance test, the number of rounds, the key length, the error-correction budget λ_EC, the error budgets ε_PA and ε_EV, and the authentication parameters ε_auth and k_auth. The Rényi order α at which the key length is computed is fixed before the run too; choosing it by comparing the key lengths your declared model gives at several orders, as the run tier's outer search over α does, reads no data of the run and is such a choice. None of them may be chosen or adjusted after looking at the run's data, for example by relaxing the acceptance threshold or picking the key length from the observed error rate. That would be a variable-length protocol, which this analysis does not cover.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Privacy amplification uses an ideal two-universal family, collision probability exactly 2^−ℓ for distinct inputs, and error verification a two-universal family. The first is what leftover hashing reads, the second what the verification collision bound reads.
assumptions.title: Ideal two-universal privacy amplification
assumptions.user_statement: Privacy amplification uses a hash family in which any two different inputs collide with probability exactly 2^−ℓ (an ideal two-universal family, such as Toeplitz hashing), and error verification uses a two-universal hash family. If your privacy-amplification family is only two-universal (collision probability at most 2^−ℓ), shorten the key by one further bit.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: On an honest run each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything before it, stays inside the declared honest envelope. The premise bears on the advertised honest abort probability and restricts no adversary.
assumptions.title: Honest rounds inside a declared envelope
assumptions.user_statement: When no attacker is present, each round's probability of each acceptance outcome, given everything that happened before, stays inside the honest model: between the lower and upper bounds of the honest envelope where you declared one, and equal to the honest distribution where you gave a single one instead (an envelope of zero width). With an envelope the channel may drift within and between runs as long as it stays inside it; with a single distribution it may not drift at all. This premise only bears on the advertised probability that an honest run aborts; it never affects security. If drift can leave the honest model, declare a wider envelope.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: On the Band-A route the declared receiver is an exactly projective qubit measurement with unit efficiency and no loss, dark counts, multi-photon events or misalignment, on a transmitted system that is exactly a qubit. The route is an explicit idealization, not a squashing argument.
assumptions.title: Ideal qubit receiver on the Band-A route
assumptions.user_statement: Only for an idealised Band-A analysis: your receiver is a perfect qubit measurement, with unit detection efficiency, no loss, no dark counts, no multi-photon events and no misalignment, and what reaches it in each round is exactly one qubit. The engine refuses a Band-A declaration whose own numbers contradict this: more than one measuring station, a measured system (or, with a trusted source, a transmitted system) of dimension other than two, or a measurement not made of projectors (per basis, where a basis choice is declared). No real optical receiver meets this; use the route to reproduce textbook comparison values. Declare a real device through the receiver module and a squashing reduction.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The post-processing acts on the raw-key string the rounds write, the declared holder computes that string, and reconciliation runs one way from the holder through a padded fixed-length transcript. The leakage term counts the register's full length.
assumptions.title: Dedicated key register and one-way reconciliation
assumptions.user_statement: Error correction is one-way. The key holder computes its raw key from its own record (its letters, the detection results of its measuring stations, or both, whichever it holds) and the public announcements, and its messages depend only on that raw key and public random seeds. The transcript always has exactly λ_EC bits, shorter messages being padded. Interactive error correction (for example Cascade) or a variable-length transcript is not covered by this key length.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Nothing about a party's records leaves its laboratory but its key, the public messages and, in trusted-source mode at the party of A, the emitted systems; the adversary acts on it only through what its declared measurements receive and the messages. It excludes side channels at both parties.
assumptions.title: Each party's laboratory is sealed
assumptions.user_statement: Whatever a party's role, nothing about its letters, settings, choices, detection results, keys or random numbers leaves its laboratory but the final key, the public messages and, where the party sends with a trusted source, the signals that source emits; timing and auxiliary signals reveal no more. An untrusted source counts as outside every laboratory, even one it is in. The attacker reaches a laboratory only via the systems its declared measurements receive and the public messages. Light sent in to read out a letter, a setting, a choice or a detector state (a Trojan-horse attack, at a receiver as at a modulator), emanations from any device, detector back-flash and anything but the declared input modes influencing a measurement violate this, a clock or trigger line from an untrusted source included; where it sends with a trusted source, so does light seeding or recalibrating its laser.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Some feasible state of the consuming declaration produces a law of the declared honest envelope, for a single declared law that law itself. It rules out an incompatibility of the honest model with the declaration.
assumptions.title: An honest law produced by a feasible state
assumptions.user_statement: Your honest model fits your protocol declaration: a state the declaration admits as feasible produces acceptance statistics in your declared honest envelope, or equal to your single declared honest law. If it fails, the declared devices do not describe the statistics and a key length for them is not warranted. The engine's own honest models are built to match the declared Alice marginal; nothing proves this premise for them. Unless switched off, the engine checks every run whose honest statistics you supply or whose declaration carries a constraint you declared: from a proven mismatch it states a cap on the probability that devices behaving as the declaration says pass your acceptance test, and refuses the run where that cap is at most one half, a threshold you can set. On an unchecked run a mismatch goes undetected and this premise is yours to vouch for.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The same specification, source mode and operators describe every round: the sameness clause of round homogeneity, not the absence of memory across rounds. One compiled declaration and one certificate decision then serve the whole run.
assumptions.title: Round homogeneity of the declaration
assumptions.user_statement: One protocol description covers the whole run. Every round uses the same measurements, the same setting choices and their probabilities, and the same classical processing, and, where the source is trusted, the same source, so one declaration and one certificate decision apply to all n rounds. A run in which you change settings, or your devices drift so that later rounds need different operators, violates this. Only parts of a run fixed before it starts, each processed as its own execution and composed under [[A-SEPARATE]], which also asks that no device carry a state from one part into the next, can be analysed separately; a split chosen after seeing the data is not covered. That no device remembers earlier rounds is not part of this premise: for the measuring stations it is [[A-SPEC]], for Alice's letter [[A-ALICE-MEAS]], and where the source is trusted the source premise.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: The post-processing seeds are drawn with their declared laws, privately, independently and afresh; in trusted-source mode the source's letters and prepared systems are independent of the adversary, who never gets a purification of them. Leftover hashing and source replacement rest on it.
assumptions.title: Private, independent and fresh local randomness
assumptions.user_statement: Your random choices come from a good private random number generator. The error-correction seed, the error-verification hash and the privacy-amplification hash are each drawn with their intended distribution, kept secret until the protocol announces them, independent of each other, of every other record of the protocol (the raw key included) and of everything the attacker knows, and drawn anew in every run. With a trusted source, the randomness with which it picks each round's letter and prepares its state is uncorrelated with the attacker at the start, and no purification of a prepared state is ever available to the attacker. A seed reused across runs, fixed in the device or disclosed early, or a predictable or pre-shared random source, violates this.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Each round runs the delivery of its quantum systems, then every party's measurement, then the round's public messages, then sifting; each party measures in round order, post-processing follows all rounds and every message is public. It is the timing premise of the security analysis.
assumptions.title: Sequential round structure
assumptions.user_statement: In every round the quantum systems come first: where your source is trusted, it prepares and sends that round's signal, and otherwise the systems of the round are delivered to the measuring stations. Then every party that measures completes its measurement, and only then are that round's public messages sent, in the declared order. Sifting is then determined by the announcements, and no operation on a quantum system of a round depends on a public message of that round. All classical post-processing (for example error correction, verification and privacy amplification) runs after all n rounds, and every classical message is public. A message sent before a measurement of the same round has finished (for example an early basis announcement) violates this. Each party that measures completes its measurement of each round before it completes that of the next round.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: Declared dimensions, alphabets, tables and measurements describe the apparatus: the receiver's in every round whatever the others did and, where no source certificate is demanded, Alice's of two or more letters; every input yields a key. The compiler checks only the last, in part.
assumptions.title: Specification faithful to the apparatus
assumptions.user_statement: Your declared numbers describe your apparatus: each system has its declared dimension, every alphabet and table (announcements, sifting, the raw key bit) is what your devices and software do, and the key rule yields a key value, never "no key", on every input. Each measuring station, of either party, performs exactly its declared measurement in every round, on that round's input alone; afterpulsing or a dead time violates this. A declared receiver instrument's measurement is the model the engine emits from it; the emission step is recorded, not bounded. Where no source-replacement certificate is demanded (an untrusted source, or a one-dimensional A), Alice's declared measurement of her letter is the one she performs; [[A-ALICE-MEAS]] adds every round, alone. The engine checks that the declaration is well formed, not that it matches your hardware.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

assumptions.summary: In trusted-source mode the retained system A stays in the laboratory of the party that holds it and is acted on only by that party's declared measurement, condition (SR3) of the certificate. It is what lets a declared marginal delete attacks.
assumptions.title: Retention of the system A in trusted-source mode
assumptions.user_statement: The source's retained half, system A, never leaves the laboratory of the party the declaration assigns it to, and nothing acts on it except that party's own declared measurement: no other step of the protocol and no action of the adversary. In a prepare-and-measure setup A exists only in the source-replacement description, and this is the premise that the adversary has no access to that party's laboratory. Only then may you declare the source's reduced state τ_A (trusted-source mode), which removes attacks from the analysis when A has dimension at least two. If you cannot vouch for this, use untrusted-source mode: the key rate can only drop, and the result stays valid.
assumptions.verification_sentence: The engine does not verify this assumption; a run that rests on it records it as unverified.

detail.accumulation_rule: maximum over the CONTRIBUTING iterates of the first-order linearization O^J_alpha(x_t) + <g_t, v_t - q_t> + b^F_t - <G_t, J_t> of Eq. eq:hlb with the lower bounds of Theorem thm:firstorder (iv): v_t the exact acceptance-side minimiser and b^F_t the feasible-side bound of Lemma lem:feasible-side-dual, verified exactly from the oracle's dual (req:verified-feasible-side) and rounded toward -inf, over every iterate the loop formed at which (H-POS), (H-SUPP) and (H-NOPERT) held and the point was established to lie in AcceptSet x Feas^J(epsilon). Under those hypotheses each bracket is a lower bound on h_low IN EXACT REAL ARITHMETIC (Theorem thm:firstorder (iiib), (iv)), and the maximum of lower bounds is a lower bound. An iterate failing any of them CONTRIBUTES NO BRACKET; the oracle's return and status withdraw none

detail.reason: certified_reported: the bracket was formed again at the run's final points from the declaration's data with every arithmetic step exact or rigorously enclosed (frank-wolfe/req:certified-evaluation), and the key length is computed exactly from max{0, h_cert} by frank-wolfe/cor:certified-keylength; the first-order number and its key length are recorded beside it
